title: Homotopy invariance of proper signed-word colimits
statement:
Let $\mathcal I$ be the small category whose objects are finite words in $+,-$, including the empty word, and whose morphisms $f:w\to v$ are weakly order-preserving maps between the sets of letter positions such that each position and its image have the same sign. Composition is composition of these maps. An injection means such a morphism injective on positions. For two injections $f:w\to v$ and $g:w'\to v$, let $h:w''\to v$ be the injection whose image is $\operatorname{im}f\cap\operatorname{im}g$, with signs inherited from $v$. A functor $E:\mathcal I\to\mathrm{sSet}$ [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set] is proper if $E(f)$ is degreewise injective for every injection $f$, and
$$\operatorname{im} E(h)=\operatorname{im} E(f)\cap\operatorname{im} E(g)\subseteq E(v)$$
for every such pair. Let $E,E'$ be proper functors and $\eta:E\to E'$ a natural transformation. If every $\eta_w$ is a weak homotopy equivalence, then
$$\varinjlim_{\mathcal I}E\longrightarrow\varinjlim_{\mathcal I}E'$$
is a weak homotopy equivalence. Here colimits have the universal property of [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] and can be formed degreewise by the quotient of the disjoint union by the diagram relations. A weak homotopy equivalence means a map whose geometric realization is bijective on path components and induces isomorphisms on all homotopy groups at every basepoint.

source.place: Section 4.1, Definition 4.4 and Proposition 4.5, printed pp. 22-23 (PDF pp. 6-7); signed-word notation for the same indexing category. No Stacks tag states this simplicial homotopy-theoretic result.

proof.text: Use the Kan model structure of [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper]; every simplicial set is cofibrant since its initial map is degreewise injective. Apply [lem-coef-reedy-model-structure] to each of three indexing categories: a discrete pair; the sequence $0\to1\to\cdots$ with degree its index and only direct arrows; and the span $X\leftarrow A\to B$ with degrees $0,1,2$ respectively, the arrow $A\to X$ inverse and $A\to B$ direct. For a base (trivial) fibration $p:U\to V$, its constant diagram is a Reedy (trivial) fibration: the relative matching maps are $p$ at every object in the discrete and sequence cases; in the span case they are $p$ at $X,B$ and the identity $U\to V\times_V U$ at $A$. The colimit/constant-diagram adjunction, obtained from the colimit universal property, identifies lifting squares and their fillers. Hence the colimit functor on each of these diagram model categories preserves cofibrations and trivial cofibrations, by their lifting characterizations.

source.place: Supporting model-category argument for Proposition 4.5: Hovey Theorem 5.2.5, Corollary 5.1.6 and proof of Lemma 5.2.6.

proof.text: Here is the weak-equivalence consequence, without appealing to a further colimit-comparison theorem. Let $u:D\to D'$ be an objectwise weak equivalence between cofibrant diagrams in any of the three model categories of Step 1. The cofibrant clause of [lem-coef-brown-split-factorizations] gives $u=pi$, $ps=1$, with $i,s$ cofibrations and $p$ a trivial fibration. Two-out-of-three makes $i,s$ trivial cofibrations. Step 1 makes $\operatorname{colim}i$ and $\operatorname{colim}s$ weak equivalences; the equation $(\operatorname{colim}p)(\operatorname{colim}s)=1$ makes $\operatorname{colim}p$ a weak equivalence by two-out-of-three, and so makes $\operatorname{colim}u$ a weak equivalence. For a discrete pair every diagram is cofibrant. For the span, cofibrancy means that $X,A$ are cofibrant and $A\to B$ is a cofibration. For a sequence it means that the initial object is cofibrant and every successor map is a cofibration, because the latching object at $n>0$ is its predecessor. Thus we have proved the coproduct, one-cofibration pushout, and monomorphic-sequence comparisons needed below.

source.place: Supporting argument for Proposition 4.5: Brown split-factorization argument; Hovey Lemma 5.2.6 and Corollary 5.1.6.

proof.text: Put $C_n(E)=\varinjlim_{\mathcal I_{\leq n}}E$, where $\mathcal I_{\leq n}$ contains words of length at most $n$. A compatible family of cocones on these full subcategories is exactly a cocone on $\mathcal I$: every object occurs in a truncation, and an arrow occurs as soon as both its endpoints do. The colimit universal property therefore gives $\varinjlim_n C_n(E)\cong\varinjlim_{\mathcal I}E$. The construction applied to $E'$ gives its corresponding isomorphism, and the universal property identifies the map under these isomorphisms with $\varinjlim_n C_n(\eta)$.

The sole object of $\mathcal I_{\leq0}$ is the empty word, so $C_0(\eta)=\eta_\epsilon$ is a weak equivalence. For $n\geq1$ use [lem-coef-signed-word-boundary-pushout] for both proper functors. Its squares attach $E(a_n^+)\amalg E(a_n^-)$ along $B_n^+(E)\amalg B_n^-(E)$ to $C_{n-1}(E)$, and give a map of squares under $\eta$. Each left attaching map is degreewise injective. In a degreewise set pushout along an injection, distinct elements of the other summand cannot be identified: each element of the injected domain has only one preimage. Thus every $C_{n-1}(E)\to C_n(E)$ is degreewise injective. This argument also gives degreewise injectivity for every transition of $C_n(E')$.

source.place: Section 4.1 Proposition 4.3 and Definition 4.4, printed pp. 22-23.

proof.text: For a word $v$ and a subset $T$ of its positions, let $v|T$ be the subword with the induced signs, and let $X_T(E)$ be the image of $E(v|T)\to E(v)$. Properness identifies $X_T(E)$ with $E(v|T)$ and gives $X_S(E)\cap X_T(E)=X_{S\cap T}(E)$. In each simplicial degree, intersection distributes over a finite union. Consequently the intersection of $X_T(E)$ with a union of subword images $X_{S_j}(E)$ is the union of the images $X_{S_j\cap T}(E)$, also viewed inside $E(v|T)$. These identifications commute with faces, degeneracies and $\eta$, since the subword injections compose as inclusions of subsets.

source.place: Definition 4.4(ii), printed p. 23; degreewise set identities.

proof.text: We prove that $\eta$ induces a weak equivalence on every finite union $\bigcup_{T\in\mathcal A}X_T(E)$ by induction first on the maximum cardinality $r$ of the subsets and then on the number $k$ of inclusion-maximal subsets. The empty family gives the identity of the empty simplicial set. A nonempty family with $r=0$ has union $X_\varnothing(E)\cong E(\epsilon)$, so the assertion is $\eta_\epsilon$. Remove contained subsets without changing the union. Choose a maximal subset $T$ of cardinality $r$, and let $U$ be the union of the other maximal images. The comparison on $U$ follows from the induction on $k$ (or the outer induction if its maximum cardinality drops); the comparison on $X_T$ is $\eta_{v|T}$. By Step 5, $U\cap X_T$ is the union for the family $S\cap T$ over the other maximal $S$. Every such intersection has cardinality less than $r$, so the outer induction gives its comparison. The square with corners $U\cap X_T,U,X_T,U\cup X_T$ is a pushout degreewise: two maps agreeing on the intersection give exactly one map on the union. Both intersection inclusions are monomorphisms. Apply the one-cofibration pushout comparison proved in Steps 1-2 (using [lem-coef-reedy-model-structure] and [lem-coef-brown-split-factorizations]) to conclude for the full union. This proves the claim, in particular for each $B_n^e(E)\to B_n^e(E')$.

source.place: Definition 4.4 and the finite-union induction implicit in Proposition 4.5, printed p. 23; induction written explicitly by the second reader.

proof.text: Induct on $n$ to prove $C_n(\eta)$ a weak equivalence. The base case is Step 4. At $n\geq1$, Step 6 gives the weak equivalences on both boundary unions and the hypotheses give $\eta_{a_n^+},\eta_{a_n^-}$. The discrete-pair comparison of Steps 1-2 gives weak equivalences on the coproducts of the two boundaries and on the coproducts of the two word-values. The third corner $C_{n-1}(\eta)$ is a weak equivalence by induction. In the two natural pushout squares of [lem-coef-signed-word-boundary-pushout], the boundary-to-word-value map is monomorphic. The span comparison proved in Steps 1-2 therefore gives the weak equivalence on their fourth corners $C_n(E)\to C_n(E')$.

source.place: Proposition 4.5 deduced from Proposition 4.3, printed p. 23.

proof.text: The two sequences $C_n(E)$ and $C_n(E')$ have cofibrant initial objects and monomorphic successor maps by Step 4. They are cofibrant diagrams in the direct sequence Reedy model structure: the latching object is initial at zero and is $C_{n-1}$ at $n>0$. Their comparison is objectwise a weak equivalence by Step 7. Apply the sequence comparison proved in Steps 1-2 from [lem-coef-reedy-model-structure] and [lem-coef-brown-split-factorizations] to obtain a weak equivalence on their sequential colimits. Step 3 identifies this map with the asserted map of full signed-word colimits.

source.place: Propositions 4.2 and 4.5, printed pp. 22-23; sequential comparison justified by the direct Reedy model structure.
